description: The Gujarat High Court has restricted AI use in judicial decision-making, highlighting risks of bias, privacy breaches, and lack of human judgement. While AI can aid research and case management, courts emphasise human responsibility. With 50 million pending cases, experts call for balanced adoption alongside systemic reforms.
body_lead: There is considerable expectation that Artificial Intelligence (AI) will contribute significantly to cut the staggering burden of pending court cases, but some High Courts are rightly cautioning against looking at it as a panacea. The Gujarat High Court recently published a policy that prohibits the use of AI for adjudication, legal reasoning, judicial decision-making, issuing a substantive order, judgment drafting, and bail or sentencing considerations.
